findings.title: Fixed-host override validation does not require a booking to fit inside an override window
findings.body: The callback marks a slot unavailable only when it is wholly before an override or starts strictly after it; any slot overlapping either edge falls through `dateOverrideExist` and is accepted. For example, a 30-minute slot from 10:45 to 11:15 is accepted for a 10:00 to 11:00 override. The `.find` also stops on the first nonmatching range, so with 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00 overrides, a valid 14:00 slot is rejected because it is after the first range. Additionally, the empty-override branch at line 114 compares two distinct Dayjs objects with `===`, so a 10:00-10:00 blackout is not detected and can admit a slot beginning at 10:00. This can book a round-robin event while its fixed host is unavailable; the code needs to require the full slot interval to be contained in at least one override range.

findings.title: Fixed-host working-hours validation rejects split schedules and permits slots past closing time
findings.body: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` rather than `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts before the end of a host's hours but finishes after it is treated as valid. Also, using `workingHours.find` with an "outside this interval" predicate makes every slot invalid for a host with multiple windows on the same day: a 10:00 slot in a 09:00-12:00 window is rejected when the 13:00-17:00 window is inspected, and vice versa. Since this check is the new fixed-host guard after round-robin availability has been aggregated, it can both hide valid slots and allow bookings that overrun a fixed host's availability. The check should test the actual slot end and accept when any applicable working-hours range fully contains the slot.

findings.title: Date-override end times use the start-time timezone offset across DST transitions
findings.body: `offset` is derived only from `override.start` and is reused when converting `override.end`. An override can span a daylight-saving transition, where the endpoint has a different organizer or invitee UTC offset. For example, a New York override from 01:00 to 03:00 on the spring-forward date spans 06:00 to 07:00 UTC, but applying the start's UTC-05 offset to the 03:00 endpoint converts it to 08:00 UTC and exposes an extra unavailable hour. Resolve the organizer/invitee offset separately for each endpoint (using the override's local date/time) before calculating its local minutes.

findings.title: The primary fixed-host round-robin behavior has no automated regression test
findings.body: The new test exercises a personal event with one user. The existing round-robin test uses `hosts: []`, which means its round-robin users are all classified as non-fixed and never execute the new `fixedHosts.every(...)` path. There is therefore no test for the reported scenario of a round-robin event with both a fixed host and a loose host, where a loose host creates a candidate slot outside the fixed host's date override. Add that scenario and assert that slots outside the fixed host's override are absent.
